audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages (p.96 penultimate root stress; p.98 Main Stress rule (70) and Secondary stress rule (72)) are verbatim on the rendered page images of the NUSA 33 scan we hold, at the stated pages. The secondary-stress rule and examples (71) match the catalog rule string exactly (initial secondary only when at least one syllable separates it from the penultimate primary). (2) Deciding source is a dedicated 47-pp phonology article (1991) by long-term SIL fieldworkers; Glottolog 5.1 lists no reference grammar or later phonology for Coastal Konjo, and the one modern theoretical paper with Konjo data (Basri, Broselow & Finer, held under sela1260) restates penultimate primary stress and clitic extrametricality, silent on secondary stress. OLAC 429; SIL 403); list of works to obtain is limited to Friberg 1995 CAD

sources.quote: 'Stress in all three languages normally falls on the penultimate syllable, regardless of syllable makeup ... Stress may be analyzed as the realization of a bisyllabic trochaic foot aligned with the right edge of the PWd ... true suffixes fall inside the stress domain while phrasal clitics fall outside it'; monomorphemic antepenultimate stress only with a final epenthetic vowel. No statement on secondary stress.
